source.title: Towards Large Scale Transfer Learning for Differentially Private Image Classification
source.authors: Harsh Mehta; Abhradeep Thakurta; Alexey Kurakin; Ashok Cutkosky

record.file_problem: Text contains the full paper, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests optimizer and batch-size effects on privately fine-tuned, pretrained ImageNet classifiers, an extension of the mapped optimization and batch-size findings to DP transfer learning.
record.gate_note: Rows capture the study's own ImageNet test-accuracy comparisons across optimizers, batch sizes, model sizes, and initialization. Cited findings from earlier large-batch studies are not recorded as rows. It does not test random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, convolutional versus fully connected generalization, dropout, sharpness measures, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares held-out ImageNet accuracy across optimizers and batch sizes in pretrained models, with and without differential privacy. These results test V4 and V5 in a transfer-learning setting. It is not an original source for either version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the scaling and optimizer conclusions but omits the main efficiency result: combining large public pretraining, a suitable optimizer, and near-zero classifier initialization enables 81.7% private ImageNet accuracy with only one full-batch last-layer update. The authors report improvements across their tested privacy budgets and leave extension beyond ImageNet to future work.
record.recipe_differences: Studies DP fine-tuning of JFT-pretrained ResNet (BiT) and ViT models on ImageNet, comparing DP and non-private Momentum/LAMB over large batches; it does not use the original studies' natural-label-from-scratch setup or test random labels.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with privacy, optimizer, batch size, model family/size, and full-model versus last-layer tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger pretrained models and more pretraining data improve private ImageNet accuracy and generally narrow its gap to the best non-private accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scaling public pretraining can improve the privacy–utility tradeoff in private image-classification transfer learning.

fits_no_version.finding: Near-zero classifier initialization enables private last-layer learning; standard LeCun initialization yields chance accuracy in the reported setting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Private last-layer fine-tuning can depend strongly on the scale of classifier initialization.

record.problems: The paper simulates a sensitive dataset using public ImageNet; JFT pretraining data are not publicly available. The optimizer exploration tunes only learning rate in the main comparisons; the authors note other hyperparameters may have different optima. Table 1 excludes ResNet50x4 full fine-tuning because accuracy did not exceed 20% even without privacy. No uncertainty estimates are given for the reported table values.
record.rows_left_out: Rows focus on the optimizer and batch-size claims. Tables 1–3 include other full/last-layer accuracy cells, but many are redundant with the extracted comparisons or model/data-scaling findings; the six-row limit does not apply, but the 60-row cap required omitting additional Table 3 full versus last-layer entries and related repeated model-size cells.

untested.parts: No fixed random-label fitting or comparison of natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
No width sweep beyond a measured zero-training-error threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected classifier comparison or local-connectivity intervention.

No language benchmarks, training-performance comparison, Adam-to-SGD switching, or controlled decoupled-weight-decay intervention. Full-model LAMB comparisons also involve a pretrained-layer learning-rate multiplier and a different decay schedule.
No language models or systematic longer-training, normalization, or regularization remedy comparison. The principal batch sweeps cover extreme batches during pretrained-model fine-tuning.
No dropout intervention; dropout is disabled.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or ranking of generalization gaps.
No identification and removal of memorized training examples.

missing.what: Direct optimizer ablation: DP-LAMB and DP-Adam both achieve 81.0%, versus 77.2% for DP-Momentum on ViT-H/14-4b last-layer fine-tuning.
Non-private one-step full-batch optimizer comparison explicitly favors LAMB/Adam over Momentum; numerical curve values cannot be recovered from the supplied text.

Add within-LAMB batch comparisons separately from same-batch optimizer contrasts. Private ViT full accuracy is 68.2, 70.5, 70.5, 71.1; private ViT last-layer accuracy is 66.4, 69.1, 70.1, 70.6; private ResNet last-layer accuracy is 52.5, 61.7, 66.1, 68.8 across 2^17–2^20.

Add non-private within-LAMB batch comparisons across 2^17–2^20: ViT full 81.7→73.1, ViT last layer 80.7→73.3, ResNet full 83.7→72.6, and ResNet last layer 82.7→72.7. Existing optimizer contrasts do not encode these baselines.

Smaller private Momentum batches for full-model ViT-B/16 yield 45.23% at 2^15 and 58.6% at 2^16, versus 66.5% at 2^17. Together with the later decline, this establishes a non-monotonic batch-size response.
missing.locator: Appendix E.4, Table 9, together with Table 1

record.verdict_notes: Table 1 was systematically misread: it contains eight batch-specific columns and no Best column. Tables 2 and 3 do contain Best columns. All principal sweeps use ten epochs; fixed privacy budgets require changing the noise multiplier with batch size. The main text says only learning rate was tuned, but Appendix D.2 additionally lists a pretrained-layer learning-rate multiplier for LAMB. Table values have no reported uncertainty; Figure 1 results are averages over five seeds.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label fitting or natural-label versus random-label generalization comparison.
No width sweep past the zero-training-error threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison on image generalization.
Does not evaluate the stated image and language benchmark range or broader optimizer tuning; studies DP transfer learning on ImageNet and includes limited learning-rate tuning.
Does not test language models; batch-size effects are studied on pretrained ImageNet classifiers, with fixed-epoch comparisons in the main sweeps.
No dropout intervention comparison on the fine-tuning classifiers; dropout is kept off in standard fine-tuning hyperparameters.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or other generalization-gap measure.
No identification or removal of memorized examples.
